full_text:
OpenBMB says MiniCPM-V 4.7 35B-A3B runs at 13+ tps on an 🍎 iPhone 17 Pro Max while using what it describes as just 3GB of memory.

But the 35B model isn't 3GB.

The actual phone deployment uses about 16.6GB of model files on storage:
💾 ~1.7GB main LES GGUF
👁️ ~1.1GB vision model
💾 ~13.8GB of streamed expert weights

How?

Flash becomes another tier of model memory.
OpenBMB’s iPhone app runs through llama.cpp-omni and keeps the routed MoE experts as separate Q3 shards on flash.

LES predicts which experts the next layer will probably need and starts loading them before they're required.
📱 Flash → most expert weights
🧠 RAM → current working set/cache
⚡ LES → hide storage latency

The actual router still decides which experts run.
So we're entering a weird new place in Local AI where:
model size ≠ required resident RAM

⚠️ OpenBMB advertises 3GB memory, but its deployment guide recommends a 12GB iPhone 17 Pro Max and ~17GB free storage.

full_text:
A ~14.5GB local agent model is doing 184 tps on an 🍎 M5 Max... and Liquid says it leads or matches the larger Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on 5 of 8 agent/tool benchmarks.

And only 2B parameters are active per token.

Liquid released LFM2.5-24B-A2B, built specifically for local agents.
🧠 24B total / 2B active
📚 131K context
💾 Q4_K_M → 14.5GB
🍎 M5 Max → 184 tps
🔴 Ryzen AI Max+ 395 → 114 tps
🧠 reasoning model
🔧 trained inside real agent harnesses

And Liquid says it is competitive with the much larger Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on agent/tool-use tasks.

Some of their reported results:
LiveClaw
LFM → 48.09
Qwen → 38.19

AutomationBench
LFM → 27.69
Qwen → 8.72

ToolSandbox
LFM → 80.71
Qwen → 75.02

They didn't just train it to answer questions.

Post-training put it inside OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Pi and OpenCode, where it learned tool calls and multi-step agent work.

And you can run it now on
llama.cpp | GGUF | MLX | vLLM | SGLang | ONNX

Base + post-trained weights are downloadable.

⚠️ Benchmark numbers are Liquid AI's own results for now. Qwen still wins several harder knowledge/coding benchmarks.

🚨Oh SiPeed took a shot directly at DGX Spark. Claims better than DGX Spark!  Faster decode on Qwen 27B at HALF the price (new or old price I don't know).

Their new MaixStation packs
🧠 128GB LPDDR5X
🚀 273 GB/s memory bandwidth
⚡ AX8860 NPU — 256 TOPS native FP4
🔋 40W compute module

And Sipeed claims on Qwen 27B:
🟢 DGX Spark → baseline
🔥 MaixStation → 25% faster prefill
🔥 MaixStation → 30% faster decode

💰 Sipeed says MaixStation will cost almost half the price of DGX Spark.
Same 128GB memory capacity.
Same 273 GB/s bandwidth.

And this isn't locked, Sipeed says it will support
⚙️ vLLM
⚙️ SGLang
⚙️ PyTorch
🐧 custom Linux distributions

It also has high-speed chip-to-chip connectivity for clustering, with Sipeed talking about systems scaling to multiple nodes without needing an expensive external 400G switch.

Samples are expected next month, with the NPU toolchain due by the end of this month.

⚠️ The Qwen performance and price comparisons are Sipeed's own claims. No independent MaixStation benchmarks yet.
